nodes.label: Janet Left-Step Periodic Table, closed at element 120
nodes.source_file: drive/The Method Materials/Conceptual idea, what if each side corresponds to ....md
nodes.rationale: Elements ordered strictly by Madelung (n + l) filling, so periods come in pairs and 2(1²+1²+2²+2²+3²+3²+4²+4²) = 120; element 120 (8s²) is the natural boundary where the f-block sequence completes.

nodes.label: Disdyakis triacontahedron (d120)
nodes.source_file: drive/The Method Materials/Conceptual idea, what if each side corresponds to ....md
nodes.rationale: 120 identical scalene-triangle faces and full icosahedral symmetry I_h with exactly 120 symmetry operations, giving a 1-to-1 face-to-element map; 62 vertices in three degree classes (12 order-10, 20 order-6, 30 order-4).

nodes.label: Spiral quantum-latitude element-to-face mapping
nodes.source_file: drive/The Method Materials/Conceptual idea, what if each side corresponds to ....md
nodes.rationale: Latitude carries the Janet period, faces spiral by Z from H at the North Pole to Ubn at the South, and block colour-coding gives 16 s, 36 p, 40 d, 28 f faces.

nodes.label: Antipodal pairing Z ↔ 121 − Z
nodes.source_file: drive/The Method Materials/Conceptual idea, what if each side corresponds to ....md
nodes.rationale: The d120 has central symmetry, so every face has an exact opposite: H opposite Ubn, C opposite Mc, Fe opposite Am — the lightest quantum states pair against the heaviest theoretical ones.
